claims.text: A hybrid model integrating DFT-derived local mass variance, force-constant distributions, and phonon-scattering rates within machine learning will reduce lattice-thermal-conductivity prediction error by at least 30%.
The proposed model will outperform both traditional effective-medium models and simplified atomistic models.
FeCoCrMnNi is a disordered five-element high-entropy alloy with atomic-scale force-constant fluctuations.
FeCoCrMnNi has significant atomic-scale mass fluctuations that materially contribute to its phonon behavior.
The model will be trained using DFT and lattice-dynamics descriptors across a representative HEA compositional space.
Phonon transport is the dominant heat-conduction mechanism from room temperature to elevated thermal-insulation operating temperatures in the target alloys.
The model is applicable to alloys containing five to seven elements, provided they lack phase separation and ordering.
Local mass and force-constant variance mediates enhanced phonon scattering in HEAs.
Force-constant fluctuations are a dominant source of phonon scattering in FeCoCrMnNi.
Simple disorder models fail to reproduce all directional features of phonon attenuation in FeCoCrMnNi, motivating more complex models.
Adding detailed DFT-derived disorder descriptors to machine learning will more accurately represent chemical-disorder effects on phonon scattering.
The improved representation of disorder-driven scattering will increase prediction accuracy specifically in the low-thermal-conductivity regime.
The model will attain at least a 30% lower mean absolute error than conventional effective-medium theories within the designed composition and temperature range.
The approach will be valid only where chemical disorder predominates in relatively uniform multielement mixtures.
Model performance may degrade for phase-separated, ordered, or out-of-training-distribution alloys.
Experimental lattice-dynamics studies support a role for force-constant fluctuations in HEA phonon scattering.
The precise prediction improvement across HEA systems and temperatures remains unquantified.
Phonon lifetimes, linewidths, and dispersions measured by inelastic neutron or X-ray scattering can be used to benchmark the model's lattice-thermal-conductivity predictions.
Failure to achieve a 30% error reduction for more than 60% of benchmark samples will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis claims a 30% improvement over both effective-medium and simplified atomistic models, whereas the predicted outcome specifies only effective-medium theories and does not require improvement over simplified atomistic simulations.

The predicted outcome defines mean absolute error over a designed range, which is an aggregate metric, while the falsification rule applies the 30% MAE-reduction condition to a percentage of individual samples. The benchmark unit and aggregation procedure are therefore inconsistent.
